Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training required.
A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible experience in business intelligence, analytics, healthcare operations, pharmacy, supply chain, or related fields.
Experience working in the healthcare industry, preferably within an academic health system, pharmacy organization, or healthcare supply chain environment.
Expert experience with business intelligence analytics, such as SQL, BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, etc.), or ERP/procurement systems to analyze data and visualize results.
Experience supporting systemwide, multi-site, or enterprise-wide initiatives involving healthcare operations, pharmacy, strategic sourcing, or supply chain management

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, Pharmacy Initiatives, the Senior Pharmacy Intelligence and Contracting Analyst serves as the systemwide subject matter expert for pharmacy analytics, spend intelligence, and strategic sourcing initiatives across UC Health. The position collaborates with pharmacy leadership, supply chain teams, manufacturers, distributors, and other stakeholders to identify opportunities to reduce pharmaceutical purchasing costs, optimize operational performance, and advance systemwide contracting and sourcing strategies. The incumbent provides expert-level analytical leadership and consultation, leading the development of complex analytical frameworks, dashboards, forecasts, and reporting solutions that support executive decision-making and strategic business initiatives. Exercising a high degree of independence and judgment, the position influences systemwide operational, financial, and sourcing strategies through data-driven insights and recommendations. The Senior Pharmacy Intelligence and Contracting Analyst serves as a trusted advisor to UC Health leadership on pharmacy analytics, vendor performance, contract optimization, and opportunities to improve financial outcomes, operational efficiency, and organizational effectiveness.

25% Design and lead the development of complex forecasts, analyses, reports, datasets, and recommendations that support and enhance business and clinical operations. Leverage subject matter expertise to inform business strategies and support organizational goals and objectives. Provide analytical and operational support for Requests for Proposals (RFPs), contract negotiations, and pharmaceutical manufacturer relationships.

This position is governed by the terms and conditions in the agreement for the Technical Unit (TX) between the University of California and the University Professional and Technical Employees (UPTE) bargaining unit contract.

25% Manage systemwide pharmacy purchasing contracts by partnering with contracting resources and UC Health leadership to review, renew, negotiate, and execute agreements. Develop and maintain strategic relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers, wholesalers, and vendors to maximize value at both system and site levels. Coordinate initiatives related to pharmacy agreements, including performance tracking, compliance monitoring, reporting, and implementation.

20% Partner with UC Health stakeholders and analytics platform representatives to ensure the integrity, accuracy, and reliability of data used in reporting and decision-making tools. Collaborate with subject matter experts to design, develop, validate, and maintain reports and dashboards. Review and audit pharmacy spend to identify pricing variances and contract discrepancies. Develop and maintain semi-automated processes for credit and rebill requests, ensuring timely resolution and recovery of contract-related savings opportunities.

15% Prepare regular reports and presentations for stakeholders and strategic sourcing teams. Utilize data from financial, procurement, and operational systems to aggregate and analyze systemwide information that drives process improvements, financial performance, and operational outcomes. Assess the availability, suitability, and quality of complex datasets while ensuring data accuracy and integrity. Implement and monitor processes and systems that improve financial performance and measure the impact of those improvements.

15% Partner with the primary pharmacy wholesaler and Group Purchasing Organization (GPO) to address contracting, pricing, and inventory access issues across the health system. Serve as the primary liaison and escalation point for complex wholesaler and GPO-related issues, facilitating resolution and maintaining productive business relationships.
Minimum of 10 years of related experience required.
5% Limited travel may be required within California to attend and support UC Health events.
Expert knowledge of business intelligence methodologies, analytics platforms, databases, reporting tools, and industry best practices.
Knowledge of pharmaceutical purchasing, pharmacy contracting, wholesaler relationships, manufacturer programs, and group purchasing organizations (GPOs).
Demonstrated ability to design and develop analytical solutions, dashboards, and reports that support business decision-making and operational improvement.
Demonstrated emotional intelligence and ability to build productive relationships with senior leaders, clinicians, technical staff, and external partners.
Advanced analytical, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate complex information and develop actionable recommendations.
Strong project management and organizational skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities and achieve results in a complex, multi-stakeholder environment.
Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and effectively influence stakeholders across organizational boundaries.
Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex information to diverse audiences and senior leadership.
